reference_items.stem:
Get to 20 Number Game

Two children, Joan and Herbert, are learning to play a game “Get to 20.” Here are the rules for the game.

GET TO 20
RULES

Pick Tiles: Each player draws three number tiles.

Add Tiles: Each player places the three tiles to make an addition problem with the sum total closest to 20.

For example, here are four ways a player who draws [1] , [4] , and [5] could place the tiles:

  [5] [1]          [4] [5]          [1] [5]             [1]
+     [4]    or  +     [1]    or  +     [4]    or     + [5]
---------        ---------        ---------         + [4]
       55               46               19         -----
                                                       10

This player should choose to show the addition problem
  15
+  4
----
  19
because 19 is the total closest to 20.

Joan and Herbert played the game “Get to 20.”

Joan picked [2] , [7] , and [9] . Herbert picked [1] , [3] , and [6] .

C. Herbert said, “If I pick [1] , [4] , and [6] , I can make 20 two different ways.”

Show two ways Herbert could make 20 with [1] , [4] , and [6] .

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it.
